statement_record.book: Rough Definition 6.68.  For symmetric monoidal categories (C, I_C, ⊗_C) and (D, I_D, ⊗_D), a symmetric monoidal functor (F, φ) : C → D is (i) a functor F : C → D, (ii) a morphism φ_I : I_D → F(I_C), (iii) for every pair c1, c2 a morphism φ_{c1,c2} : F(c1) ⊗_D F(c2) → F(c1 ⊗_C c2) natural in c1 and c2, subject to unstated ('bookkeeping') axioms making φ compatible with the associators, unitors and symmetries.  If φ_I and all φ_{c1,c2} are isomorphisms, (F, φ) is strong.
statement_record.intree: `LaxMonoidalFunctor` supplies exactly (i)–(iii) with `lax_pure : I ~> F I` for φ_I and `lax_ap {x y} : F x ⨂ F y ~> F (x ⨂ y)` for φ_{c1,c2}, the latter defined as a component of the natural transformation `ap_functor_nat : ((⨂) ◯ F ∏⟶ F) ~> (F ◯ (⨂))` in the functor category `[C ∏ C, D]`; the three coherence equations `lax_monoidal_unit_left`, `lax_monoidal_unit_right`, `lax_monoidal_assoc` are the unitor/associator axioms.  `BraidedLaxMonoidalFunctor` adds the symmetry axiom `fmap[F] braid ∘ lax_ap ≈ lax_ap ∘ braid`.  `MonoidalFunctor` is the same data with both comparisons invertible (`pure_iso : I ≅ F I`, `ap_functor_iso`), which is the book's 'strong'.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the book declines to state the coherence axioms at all ('Rough Definition', axioms called bookkeeping), while the library writes all three out and, additionally, makes naturality of φ structural rather than a side condition — φ is the component of a morphism in `[C ∏ C, D]`, so naturality in c1 and c2 holds by construction instead of needing separate checking.  Direction matches the book (into F of the tensor, i.e. lax, not oplax).  The only presentational difference is that the library keeps the derived isos `pure_left`/`pure_right`/`ap_assoc` as fields.

statement_record.book: Theorem 6.77.  Given a category C with finite colimits and a symmetric monoidal functor (F, φ) : (C, +) → (Set, ×), there is a hypergraph category Cospan_F whose objects are the objects of C and whose morphisms A → B are the equivalence classes of F-decorated cospans, composed by (6.76); its symmetric monoidal and hypergraph (Frobenius) structure are induced by those of Cospan_C.
statement_record.intree: The whole tower is constructed — `DecoratedCospanCat` (Category), `DecoratedCospan_Bifunctor`, `DecoratedCospan_Monoidal`, `DecoratedCospan_BraidedMonoidal`, `DecoratedCospan_SymmetricMonoidal`, `DecoratedCospan_Hypergraph : @Hypergraph DC DCSMC` — but every layer is built inside a Section whose Context assumes a decoration-coherence class (`DecCospan_Coherent`, `DecCospan_Bifunctor_Coherent`, `DecCospan_Monoidal_Coherent`, `DecCospan_Braided_Coherent`, `DecCospan_Symmetric_Coherent`, `DecCospan_Hypergraph_Coherent`) supplying exactly the equations the theorem asserts.  The file's own status note (Hypergraph.v lines 91-105) states it: "NONE of these classes is instantiated anywhere in the library: only the [Class] declarations and the [Context] assumptions exist, with no [Instance]/[Build_] witnesses.  This construction is therefore a CONDITIONAL result … Even the 'trivial decoration' ([F = Δ I_D]) witness is NOT supplied here."
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the book DERIVES the category/SMC/hypergraph laws from the single hypothesis that (F, φ) is symmetric monoidal; in-tree those laws are ASSUMED, one coherence class per layer, so the implication proved is 'coherences ⇒ hypergraph category', not 'symmetric monoidal F ⇒ hypergraph category'.  The hypotheses also differ: the library needs a chosen `HasPushouts C` plus `Cocartesian C` and `Initial C` (rather than 'finite colimits'), an abstract `MC : @Monoidal C` with a `cospan_merge : N ⊗ M ~> N + M` bridge, and — for the hypergraph layer — the lax-SYMMETRIC strengthening of F, which the book's Definition 6.68 supplies but which the library encodes only indirectly through the Braided/Symmetric coherence classes. statement_record.book: Unnumbered, in running prose.  Fix the component set C := {light, switch, battery} ∪ {x Ω | x ∈ R+}.  For any set C, a C-circuit is a graph (V, A, s, t) — vertices V, edges A, source and target functions s, t : A → V — together with a labelling l : A → C assigning a component to each edge; so a C-circuit is a 5-tuple (V, A, s, t, l).  Distinct tuples can denote the same physical circuit (reversing an edge).
statement_record.intree: `Quiver` gives the graph half in indexed form: `nodes : Type` for V and `edges : nodes → nodes → Type` for the fibres of (s, t) : A → V × V, with each fibre a setoid.  Nothing carries a labelling, and no record named for a circuit (or any C-tuple) exists.
